Goal: Electron refactor into Node.JS server + Browser for UI

It seem that having a dedicated Elector app instead of just running the UI over a browser has no advantages. Just to opposite, I have to also implement a browser to browser inside. I want to understand what it would take for us to transition away from electon into Server + Render App UI

## Verdict

Feasible, and your instinct is right on the biggest point: **the "browser inside the app" tab is the strongest single argument for the move.** But the work is not small, and the cost isn't where you'd expect. Electron API coupling is *shallow*; the transport coupling is *wide*.

Measured on the current tree:

| Surface | Size |
|---|---|
| `src/main/*.cjs` | 22,100 lines (+ ~70 files under `lib/`) |
| `ipcMain` channels | **171** |
| Preload namespaces | **34** (`src/preload/index.cjs`, 499 lines) |
| `window.api.*` call sites | **488** across **102** renderer files |
| `ipcRenderer` bindings in preload | 206, of which ~35 are push channels |
| Genuinely Electron-only APIs | **~12 call sites** |

That last row is the headline. Almost all of `src/main/` is plain Node — `fs`, `child_process`, `chokidar`, `ws`, `node-pty`. The `require('electron')` in ~35 files is overwhelmingly `app.getPath('userData'|'home')` and `ipcMain.handle`. Neither is hard to replace.

---

## 1. The genuinely Electron-coupled list (small, and fully enumerable)

| API | Where | Browser replacement |
|---|---|---|
| `app.getPath` | ~everywhere | `os.homedir()` — trivial, mechanical |
| `ipcMain.handle` × 171 | everywhere | see §2 |
| `WebContentsView` (12) | `browserView.cjs` (916 L), `browserCapture.cjs` (728 L) | **the hard one** — see §4 |
| `dialog.showOpen/Save/MessageBox` (3) | `index.cjs:494,513,616` | in-app picker over an fs API. Real work; there's no native folder picker on the web. `showDirectoryPicker` is Chromium-only + can't be seeded to a path |
| `globalShortcut` | `voiceHotkey.cjs` | **lost.** No web equivalent |
| `clipboard.readImage/readText` | `index.cjs:529–579` | partially lost — you added main-process clipboard *specifically* because `navigator.clipboard.read()` couldn't do it (your own comment at `index.cjs:550`). Paste-events still work; on-demand reads don't |
| `protocol.handle('smfile://')` | `index.cjs:1056` | an HTTP route — actually simpler |
| `session.defaultSession` CSP + permission handlers | `index.cjs:1036,1078` | server response headers. Simpler |
| `shell.openExternal/openPath/showItemInFolder/trashItem` (11) | various | `openExternal` → `<a target=_blank>`; the other three are **server-side `xdg-open`/`open`**, which is fine for localhost and meaningless for remote |
| `Menu.popup` | `index.cjs:402` | you already have a DOM context-menu ladder (`zLayers.ts`) — fold into it |
| `powerMonitor` suspend/resume | `crashDiagnostics.cjs`, `scheduler.cjs:4749` | Node has no equivalent; approximate with a clock-drift detector |
| `systemPreferences.askForMediaAccess` | darwin mic | browser prompts natively. **Better** |

Voice survives: `vad-web` / `onnxruntime-web` / whisper workers are all already renderer-side (`turnDetectorWorker.ts`, `whisperWorker.ts`), and `localhost` is a secure context so `getUserMedia` works. You lose only the *global* hotkey, not voice itself.

## 2. The actual bulk of the work: the transport

171 channels × request/response + ~35 push channels. The move is:

- **Preload → client shim.** `window.api` is the only boundary the renderer knows (zero `ipcRenderer` imports in `src/renderer/` — I checked). So you rewrite **one file**, `src/preload/index.cjs`, into a browser module that keeps the identical 34-namespace shape but dispatches over `fetch` + one WebSocket. **488 call sites don't change.** This is the single best structural fact about your codebase for this refactor.
- **`ipcMain.handle` → route table.** You already have the pattern twice: `lib/localAdminHttp.cjs` (loopback, bearer token, timing-safe compare, route registration) and `browserAgentServer.cjs`. Generalizing `localAdminHttp` into the app's real transport is the natural path — not a greenfield server.
- **`ipcSchemas.cjs` (1,061 L of zod) gets more valuable, not less.** It's currently a defence-in-depth nicety over a trusted preload; over HTTP it becomes the actual security boundary. Keep it, it's already written.
- **PTY over WebSocket.** `pty.cjs` is 315 lines and already keyed by tabId; xterm-over-WS is the ttyd/wetty pattern. Straightforward.
- **`sendIfAlive`/`sendToRenderer.cjs` → WS broadcast** with per-topic subscription. Note `broadcastCoalescer.cjs` already exists — reuse.

Estimate: this is the multi-week part. Not conceptually hard, just 171 endpoints wide.

## 3. What you actually gain

- **No `electron-rebuild`, no ~100MB Electron download.** Your own `bin/cli.cjs` has 20 lines of error copy dedicated to that download failing behind corporate proxies. That whole failure class disappears. `node-pty` still needs a native build, but against stable Node ABI with prebuilds — far less fragile than per-Electron-ABI rebuilds.
- **Web Remote v2 collapses into the main app.** `webRemote.cjs` is 1,367 lines of relay client + E2E crypto that exists *only* because the desktop UI can't be reached from a phone. Server + browser makes the phone a client of the same UI. This is arguably a bigger prize than the browser tab.
- **E2E gets simpler.** 19 Playwright-Electron specs become plain Playwright-Chromium. Also kills the `no_second_electron_while_jobs_run` hazard (screenshot runs SIGTERMing live scheduler jobs / clobbering `admin-api.json`).
- **Multi-window / multi-device for free** — several tabs on one server, which the current one-BrowserWindow model can't do.

## 4. The trap in your premise

> I have to also implement a browser inside

Careful — this doesn't fully go away, it **changes shape**. The Browser tab isn't a viewer; `browserCapture.cjs` (728 L) + `RecorderPanel`/`CapturePanel` *drive* the page. In a browser-hosted UI you cannot embed arbitrary third-party sites in an `<iframe>` — `X-Frame-Options` / `frame-ancestors` kills most real sites, and you'd have no scripting access into them anyway.

Three honest options:
1. **Delete it** — "open in your real browser." Loses capture/record.
2. **Server-side headless Chromium** (Playwright — already an MCP dep here) with screencast frames to the UI. Keeps every capability, but you're now *running* a browser rather than *embedding* one. Arguably cleaner: it becomes an automation service, not UI chrome.
3. **Proxy + rewrite** — don't. Endless.

Option 2 is the right answer, and it's a genuine improvement, but it is **new work, not deleted work**. Budget it.

## 5. The new problem you're buying: security

Today the boundary is `contextIsolation` + `validatePath(allowedRoots = homedir)`. A local HTTP server with full home-directory read/write and arbitrary `claude -p` spawn is a materially different posture:

- Bind `127.0.0.1` only, bearer token in a 0600 file, **origin/`Sec-Fetch-Site` checks on every route** (DNS-rebinding and any local webpage can `fetch()` your port otherwise).
- `validatePath` becomes load-bearing in a way it currently isn't.
- The single-writer law (`opsOwnership.cjs`) already assumes one process — good, that holds. But `instanceLock.cjs` / `singleInstanceGuard.cjs` need rethinking: the server is now the singleton and the UI is disposable.

You already have the right primitives (`localAdminHttp.cjs`'s token bootstrap + `crypto.timingSafeEqual`), which is why I'd extend it rather than write new.

## 6. Phasing I'd recommend

The key insight: **you can do this incrementally under a running Electron shell**, because Electron can load `http://127.0.0.1:PORT` instead of `dist/index.html`.

1. **Extract the server.** Move `ipcMain.handle` registration behind a transport interface; stand up the HTTP+WS server in-process. Electron keeps hosting the window, now pointed at localhost. Nothing user-visible changes; everything stays testable.
2. **Port the shim.** Rewrite preload as a dual-mode client (IPC when present, HTTP/WS otherwise). Now the app runs in Chrome *and* Electron, same code.
3. **Close the native gaps** — file picker, context menu, clipboard, `smfile` route. One PRD each.
4. **Re-home the Browser tab** onto headless Chromium (or cut it).
5. **Drop Electron.** `bin/cli.cjs` becomes `node server.cjs && open http://127.0.0.1:PORT`. Delete `webRemote.cjs`'s relay layer.

Steps 1–2 are where the value is; you could stop after 2 and already have the browser-hosted UI, keeping Electron only as an optional shell for the native niceties.

---

## What I'd want decided before decomposing this into PRDs

I can start on step 1 immediately without any of these answered — but they change the shape of steps 3–5:

1. **Is Electron kept as an optional shell, or fully deleted?** Keeping it as a thin `--desktop` wrapper preserves the global voice hotkey, clipboard reads, and native dialogs at near-zero ongoing cost, and makes the whole migration non-lossy. Deleting it entirely means accepting those losses. I'd recommend keeping it as an optional shell — but it's a real fork in the plan.
2. **Browser tab: delete, or rebuild on headless Chromium?** This is the difference between ~1,900 lines removed and ~1,900 lines rewritten.
3. **Is remote (non-localhost) access a goal, or is this strictly `127.0.0.1` + a local browser?** If remote is in scope, auth/TLS/multi-user session isolation becomes a first-class design problem rather than a token file, and it should be designed in from step 1 — not retrofitted.

(2) Start with deleting the browser-tab and related features around record and dom capture for leaniency  (3) Same with the Remote Access delete them (1) Same with Elector delete it.  All these will be in GIT when we need them, for now we are going LIGHT

Good — that simplifies the plan substantially. Deleting first is the right order, and here's why concretely: **the two surfaces you're cutting are exactly the two hardest things to port.** `WebContentsView` has no browser equivalent, and `webRemote.cjs`'s relay + E2E crypto exists solely to work around the desktop UI being unreachable. Cutting them shrinks the transport port from 171 IPC channels to **136**, and removes the headless-Chromium rebuild entirely.

## Deletion surface (measured)

| Delete | Files | Lines |
|---|---|---|
| **Browser tab** | `browserView.cjs` 916, `browserCapture.cjs` 728, `browserAgentServer.cjs` 224, `browserViewPreload.cjs` 118, `lib/browserAgentActions.cjs` 114 | 2,100 |
| ↳ renderer | `Browser.tsx` 165, `state/browser.ts` 483, + 9 files in `tabs/browser/`, `lib/captureDest.ts` | ~1,200 |
| ↳ tests | `browserView-destroyed-handler`, `browserView-oauth-popup`, `browserCapture.spec` | — |
| **Web Remote** | `webRemote.cjs` 1,367, `lib/e2eStateMachine.cjs` 39, `WebRemote.tsx` 522 | 1,928 |
| ↳ tests | `ipc-web-remote`, `webRemoteAuthGate`, `webRemoteSasState`, `web-remote-e2e-pinning` | — |
| **Total** | | **~5,200 lines, 35 IPC channels** |

## Three residual couplings — re-home, don't delete

These are the only things outside those directories that would break. All three are small and all three get *better*:

1. **`epics/attachments.tsx:105`** calls `window.api.browser.saveBinary(destPath, base64, 'epics')` — Epic image attachments borrowing the Browser namespace's IPC channel. Note it already passes `'epics'` as the ops writer and the files already land in `prompt-sessions/attachments/`. Only the channel name is browser-owned. Move `saveBinary` to the `files` namespace before deleting.
2. **`lib/handleChatLinkClick.ts` → `ChatTranscriptTurn.tsx`** opens chat links in the embedded browser. Post-delete this becomes a plain `<a target="_blank">` — strictly simpler, and it's the correct behaviour in a browser-hosted UI anyway.
3. **`opsOwnership.cjs:52`** declares `'browser': 'browser'` as an OWNERS namespace. Once (1) moves, that entry and the `session-manager-operations/browser/` folder retire. CLAUDE.md calls this out as "the one exception that IS in OWNERS" — that exception disappears, which is a real doc simplification.

Plus `navGroups.ts:52` (nav entry) and `Settings`/nav references to WebRemote.

## What deleting Electron actually costs (full list, nothing hidden)

Since you're going all the way, these are lost with no browser equivalent — I want them on the record now rather than discovered mid-port:

| Lost | Impact |
|---|---|
| **Native folder picker** (`dialog.showOpenDialog`, `index.cjs:494`) | **The one that matters.** "Open / Start Project" is the root of the whole TAB→Epic model. Must be rebuilt as a server-side directory-listing API + in-app picker. Not optional, not trivial. |
| `globalShortcut` voice hotkey (`voiceHotkey.cjs`, 351 L) | Global push-to-talk dies. In-window accelerator survives. Voice itself is unaffected — VAD/whisper are already renderer-side workers. |
| `clipboard.readImage/readText` (`index.cjs:529–579`) | On-demand clipboard *reads* die — your own comment at `:550` says these exist precisely because the web API couldn't do it. Paste **events** still work, so image-paste into Epics survives; a "read clipboard now" button would not. |
| `powerMonitor` suspend/resume | `scheduler.cjs:4749` uses `resume` to recover the queue after sleep; `crashDiagnostics.cjs` logs both. Approximate with a clock-drift detector. |
| `shell.openPath` / `showItemInFolder` / `trashItem` (8 sites) | Become server-side `xdg-open`/`open` — fine for localhost. |
| `Menu.popup`, `systemPreferences.askForMediaAccess`, `powerSaveBlocker`, `protocol('smfile')` | All have clean replacements (DOM menu via existing `zLayers.ts`; browser's own mic prompt — actually better; drop; HTTP route). |

**Gained by deletion:** no `electron-rebuild`, no 100MB binary download (kills the 20 lines of proxy-failure error copy in `bin/cli.cjs`), 19 Playwright-Electron specs become plain Chromium, and the `no_second_electron_while_jobs_run` hazard — screenshot runs SIGTERMing live scheduler jobs and clobbering `admin-api.json` — evaporates.

## PRD chain

**Phase 0 — delete (do first, independently landable, no server work)**
- **P0.1** Move `saveBinary` off the `browser` IPC namespace to `files`; retire the `browser` OWNERS namespace + folder. *Blocks P0.2.*
- **P0.2** Delete the Browser tab: 5 main/preload files, 11 renderer files, 3 test files, nav entry; rewrite `handleChatLinkClick` to `target="_blank"`.
- **P0.3** Delete Web Remote: 3 files, 4 test files, nav entry, Settings surface. Independent of P0.1/0.2 — can run in parallel.
- **P0.4** CLAUDE.md pass — remove the web-remote v2 section, the Browser/`browserAgentServer` bullets, the OWNERS `browser` exception, and the `no_second_electron_while_jobs_run` memory.

**Phase 1 — transport (the bulk)**
- **P1.1** Generalize `lib/localAdminHttp.cjs` into the app transport: HTTP routes + one WS, bearer token, `Sec-Fetch-Site`/origin checks. The pattern already exists — this is extension, not greenfield.
- **P1.2** Convert 136 `ipcMain.handle` registrations to route registrations behind a transport interface. `ipcSchemas.cjs` (1,061 L of zod) stops being defence-in-depth and becomes the real boundary — keep every line.
- **P1.3** Rewrite `src/preload/index.cjs` (499 L) as the browser client shim, same 34 namespaces. **488 call sites across 102 renderer files do not change** — the renderer has zero `ipcRenderer` imports, which is the single best structural fact here.
- **P1.4** PTY over WebSocket (`pty.cjs`, 315 L, already keyed by tabId); push channels via WS topics, reusing `lib/broadcastCoalescer.cjs`.

**Phase 2 — native gaps**
- **P2.1** In-app folder picker over a directory-listing API. *Recommend server-side listing + custom UI, not `showDirectoryPicker` — that's Chromium-only and can't be seeded to a starting path.*
- **P2.2** DOM context menu (fold into existing `zLayers.ts` ladder); `smfile://` → HTTP route; `shell.*` → server-side open.

**Phase 3 — cut the cord**
- **P3.1** Delete Electron: `bin/cli.cjs` becomes `node server.cjs` + open browser; drop `electron` + `@electron/rebuild` deps; rework `instanceLock`/`singleInstanceGuard` so the *server* is the singleton and the UI is disposable. `--simple` mode becomes a URL flag.
- **P3.2** Port 19 e2e specs from Playwright-Electron to Playwright-Chromium.

**Sequencing note:** Phase 1 can land *under* a still-running Electron shell — point `BrowserWindow` at `http://127.0.0.1:PORT` instead of `dist/index.html`. Everything stays runnable and testable at every commit; Electron is only removed in Phase 3, once the browser path is proven.

**PRD 1004 wrote to disk but did not land in `queue.json`.** The file exists with correct frontmatter (`dependsOn: [delete-browser-tab, delete-web-remote]`), but the queue holds only 3 jobs — 1001, 1002, 1003. I re-read the queue fresh to rule out a stale snapshot; it's genuinely absent.

## Root cause — scope overrun into PRD 1002, leaving a live runtime break

The executor did not stop at re-homing one method. `git show 11648cc -- src/preload/index.cjs` shows it deleted the **entire `webRemote` preload namespace** (13 methods: `getStatus`, `enable`, `disable`, `enableControl`, `disableControl`, `pair`, `revokeDevice`, `auditTail`, `revokeAll`, `confirmSas`, and the three `on*` subscriptions), plus from `ipcSchemas.cjs`: `webRemotePair`, `webRemoteRevokeDevice`, `webRemoteAuditTail`, `WEB_REMOTE_OTP_RE`, `DEVICE_ID_RE`, `READ_COMMANDS`, `SAS_GATED_READS`, `MUTATE_COMMANDS`, `ALLOWED_COMMANDS` — and unrelatedly `sessionSubscribe`. That accounts for the `api.d.ts −63` / `ipcSchemas.cjs −113` lines that a one-method re-home has no business touching.

That is PRD 1002's scope, executed **halfway**: `src/main/webRemote.cjs` still exists at that commit (53,432 bytes) and still consumes the exports that were deleted out from under it.

```
src/main/webRemote.cjs:71  const { ALLOWED_COMMANDS, MUTATE_COMMANDS, SAS_GATED_READS } = require('./ipcSchemas.cjs');
src/main/webRemote.cjs:983   if (!ALLOWED_COMMANDS.has(type)) {

$ node -e "const s=require('./src/main/ipcSchemas.cjs'); ..."
ALLOWED_COMMANDS: undefined
MUTATE_COMMANDS: undefined
SAS_GATED_READS: undefined
```
